tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Mean-value property for the heat equation] ↗ def:fundamental-solution-heat-equation ↗ def:parabolic-cylinder-heat-ball ↗ def:heat-ball 1. ch2:2.3-thm-3\group Heat Equation

If $u\in C_1^2(U_T)$ solves the heat equation, then \[ (19)\qquad u(x,t)=\frac1{4r^n}\iint _{E(x,t;r)} u(y,s)\frac{|x-y|^2}{(t-s)^2}\, dy\, ds \] whenever $E(x,t;r)\subset U_T$.
Proof

\sketch Translate $(x,t)$ to $(0,0)$, write $E(r)=E(0,0;r)$, and set

\[ \phi (r)=\frac1{r^n}\iint _{E(r)}u(y,s)\frac{|y|^2}{s^2}\, dy\, ds. \]

After scaling to $E(1)$, differentiate in $r$. With

\[ \psi =-\frac n2\log (-4\pi s)+\frac{|y|^2}{4s}+n\log r, \]

one has $\psi =0$ on $\partial E(r)$. Spatial and time integration by parts, together with $u_s-\Delta u=0$, shows $\phi '(r)=0$. The scaling identity

\[ r^{-n}\iint _{E(r)}\frac{|y|^2}{s^2}\, dy\, ds=4 \]

then gives $\phi (r)=4u(0,0)$.

□
